newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Clairvest buys NZ, Aust security assets. [CORRECTED 23:57 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Clairvest buys NZ, Aust security assets. [CORRECTED 23:57 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects denominations throughout to Australian dollars, from Canadian dollars).
Canadian investment bank Clairvest Group Inc said on Tuesday it had bought the electronic security assets of Securitas in New Zealand and of Tempo Services Ltd in Australia for A$23 million.

The purchase, through its 80-percent owned unit, Signature Security Group and its affiliates, would make Signature the second biggest electronic security company in Australasia, it said in a statement released in Toronto.
Tempo and Securitas are leading guard and security firms in their respective markets, Clairvest said.
The assets, with a combined annual revenue of about A$20 million, comprised ADT Ltd's regional operations before they were sold in 1994.
Clairvest said it had invested A$12.5 million in Signature, a partnership with former U.S. Secret Service agent Jim Covert.

Covert, president and chief executive of Signature, was the founder of SecurityLink, which was sold to Ameritech in 1994. Clairvest said Covert was a secret service agent in the White House under presidents Richard Nixon, Gerald Ford and Jimmy Carter before leading California-based API Alarm Systems Inc.

"Clairvest and Signature believe that the Australasia region presents and attractive industry opportunity due to the fragmented and under-penetrated market combined with burglary rates that double those of the United States," Clairvest said.
